# Core routing inference service, version 1, revision 1

Implement the mathematical service below. There is one input and one output per
process, no persistent state, files, sockets, external commands or randomness.
All AS numbers are integers in 1..4294967295, compared numerically.
Probability-vector slots are always `[c2p, p2p, p2c]` in the stated link direction.
Reversing a link swaps slots 0 and 2. JSON booleans are not integers.

## Input

The top-level object has exactly these keys:

```json
{"version":1,"ixps":[],"rib":[],"priors":[],"declared":[],"order":[],"queries":[]}
```

* `ixps`: a list of distinct AS numbers to remove from every path.
* `rib`: records `{"path":[ASN,...],"count":positive_integer}`. Each count is
  at most 1000000. Repeated records and reverse paths are allowed.
* `priors`: records `{"link":[u,v],"weights":[a,b,c]}` with `u != v` and three
  integer weights in 0..1000000 whose sum is positive. Normalize by their sum.
  A link may be specified in either direction. Each unordered pair appears at
  most once. Priors supply edge links and links seen only in queries; an absent
  prior means `[1/3,1/3,1/3]`. A prior for a core link is ignored.
* `declared`: records `{"link":[u,v],"rel":"c2p"}` with `u != v`;
  `rel` may also be `p2p` or `p2c`. Equal endpoints invalidate the entire
  request. Each unordered pair appears at most once. These trusted declarations
  replace probabilities with the corresponding one-hot vector **for query
  scoring only**, including links absent from the RIB. They do not condition
  inference and do not change the `links` output. A declaration wins over a prior.
* `order`: a permutation of the canonical core links, each written `[u,v]` with
  `u < v`. Its meaning and the width restriction are defined below.
* `queries`: records `{"id":"token","path":[ASN,...],"threshold":[a,b]}`.
  IDs are unique, match `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64}`, and retain input order.
  The threshold is the exact rational `a/b`, where `0 <= a <= b <= 1000000`
  and `b >= 1`.

Input size is at most 4194304 UTF-8 bytes. There are at most 2000 RIB records,
2000 priors, 2000 declarations, 512 queries and 1024 IXPs. Each raw path has
0..64 AS numbers; the sum of raw RIB path lengths is at most 40000.
There are at most 4096 distinct RIB links after normalization and at most
64 core links. JSON keys are unique; numbers in this input are integers only.
The width promise below also applies. There are no additional topology promises.

Reject any input outside this schema or these bounds, duplicate JSON keys,
malformed UTF-8/JSON, noninteger numbers or extra keys with exactly
`{"error":"invalid"}` and exit 0. Whitespace is immaterial. Infrastructure
termination due to excessive input beyond the byte bound need not be recovered.

## Normalize paths before using topology or probabilities

First remove all IXP ASNs, then collapse each maximal run of adjacent duplicate
ASNs to one ASN. If any ASN still repeats, the path has a loop.
Discard looped RIB records and RIB paths with fewer than two remaining ASNs.
Aggregate identical remaining **directed** paths by summing their counts.
The discarded records contribute neither links nor contexts. Opposite directions
are distinct observations. Prepending can become adjacent after IXP removal.

Queries use the same normalization. Return their normalized path, including
nonadjacent repeats when there is a loop. Looped queries have status `loop` and
null scores, witness and decision. Paths with 0, 1 or 2 ASNs are valid queries
with both scores 1, witness null and leaked false.

## Simultaneous topology peeling

Begin with the aggregated normalized RIB paths. A link is an unordered pair.
At round r, mark a link `{u,v}` peripheral if **one fixed endpoint** is a path
endpoint in every current path containing that link. Formally either all such
paths have u as their first or last ASN, or all such paths have v as their first
or last ASN. The endpoint may be first in one path and last in another.
Being peripheral in every occurrence with *different* outer endpoints is
insufficient. Count weights do not affect this decision.

Find all marked links from the current path set simultaneously and record their
round, starting at 1. For each path remove its first ASN if its first link is
marked and its last ASN if its last link is marked, using the pre-round path
for both decisions. Discard results of length below two; aggregate identical
trimmed directed paths by summing counts. Repeat until no marked links remain.
All surviving links are core links with round 0. Preserve every link from the
original normalized RIB in the output, even if it was removed. The final paths
and their aggregated counts define the core inference observations.

## Exact core model

There is one ternary variable X_e per canonical core link e=(u,v), u<v.
It denotes the relationship from u to v. Assignments of reverse directed links
are inverse views of this same variable, never independent variables.

For each occurrence of e in each final core path, orient the entire path so
that this occurrence traverses u then v; reverse the path if necessary.
Its context consists of the directed predecessor link ending at u and the
directed successor link starting at v. A missing predecessor has constant type
c2p; a missing successor has constant type p2c. Other context types are obtained
from their canonical variables with reversal as needed.

The preferred center type g(L,R) is this table (rows L, columns R):

| g | c2p | p2p | p2c |
|---|---|---|---|
| c2p | c2p | c2p | p2p |
| p2p | p2p | p2p | p2c |
| p2c | p2p | p2p | p2c |

For each e define `phi_e(X)` as the sum of observation counts for occurrences
whose center variable X_e equals g(L,R). Every occurrence contributes its full
aggregated path count; contexts that coincide add, they do not deduplicate.

Define `W(X) = product_e phi_e(X)` over all core links, and
`Z = sum_X W(X)` over all ternary assignments. The requested core probability
for state t is `sum_{X: X_e=t} W(X) / Z`. This is an exact joint distribution;
normalizing only phi_e, substituting neighbors' marginal modes, or sampling
with a fixed number of iterations does not implement this contract.

Every potential and Z is a finite nonnegative integer. Do not assume that a
particular assignment has positive weight: endpoint defaults can make the
all-peer weight zero. If Z is positive, compute the marginals above. If Z is
zero, return exactly `{"error":"zero-partition"}` and exit 0, with no link or
query records. This is a model outcome for a well-formed input, distinct from
`{"error":"invalid"}` for a schema/bounds/order violation. All input validation,
including the width restriction, precedes this outcome. Do not smooth, remove
observations, substitute priors or skip inference to turn Z positive; priors,
declarations and the presence or absence of queries do not change Z. If any
independent core component has zero partition, the entire request has this
outcome. With no core links, the empty product and Z equal 1 and there are no
marginals to compute. See `PARTITION.md` for the endpoint counterexample and
the reasoning for these normalization rules.

To bound exact inference, construct one scope per phi_e containing e and every
distinct nonconstant context variable in any occurrence of e. Join all variables
within each scope to form an undirected graph. Traverse `order`: connect all
current neighbors of the next variable into a clique, then remove that variable.
It has at most **4 current neighbors** at every removal. `order` must contain
every core link exactly once. This is a structural input restriction, not a
required inference algorithm. Brute force over all 64 links is unnecessary.

## Scoring and localization

For each nonlooped query, look up every directed link: declaration first, then
core marginal, then prior, then uniform. Reorient each vector to the query's
direction. These are scoring inputs; declarations never modify the core model.

For each consecutive triple starting at ASN index i (zero based), let U be
the c2p probability of its first link and D the p2c probability of its second.
Its legitimacy is `U + D - U*D`. `score` is the minimum over all triples.
`witness` is the smallest index attaining this exact minimum, including when
the minimum is 1. `leaked` is true exactly when `score < a/b`; equality is valid.
There is no rounding before comparison or witness selection.

Also return `full`, the sum of the probabilities of all link-type sequences
matching `c2p* p2c*` or `c2p* p2p p2c*`. A sequence's weight is the product of
its link probabilities. These two forms are disjoint; count each sequence once.
Both `score` and `full` use the product-of-marginals interpretation specified
here, even though core inference is joint. `full` is a diagnostic and never
controls `leaked` or `witness`. It can be smaller than `score` on long paths.

## Output and execution

For a valid input with Z > 0, return exactly
`{"version":1,"links":[...],"queries":[...]}`. The two other complete output
forms are `{"error":"invalid"}` and `{"error":"zero-partition"}` as defined
above. There are no partial successful results when Z is zero.
`links` includes exactly the canonical links of the normalized, accepted RIB,
sorted by numeric (u,v). Each record has exactly these keys:
`{"link":[u,v],"round":0,"prob":[0.2,0.3,0.5]}`.
For removed links use their peeling round and prior (or uniform) probability.
For core links use round 0 and the inferred marginal. Declarations do not appear
in or change these records.

Each query record has exactly these keys:
`{"id":"q","path":[1,2,3],"status":"ok","score":0.75,"full":0.75,"witness":0,"leaked":false}`.
Status is `ok` or `loop` only; a loop record uses null for `score`, `full`,
`witness`, `leaked`. Query results retain input order. Arrays and integer fields
must be exact; probability values must be finite JSON numbers within absolute
error 1e-8 of the exact value. Booleans and null must have the stated JSON type.
Reject extra output keys, duplicate keys, NaN/Infinity, trailing nonwhitespace,
missing/extra records, wrong status, wrong witness or wrong decisions.

Submit exactly one regular, singly linked file `submission/main.py`, at most
262144 bytes; no additional entries (including directories), symlinks, devices
or hard links. All necessary code belongs in that file. Other public workspace
files may be used during development but are not collected. The grader invokes
`python3 -I /workspace/submission/main.py` with a fresh process per input.
Use the standard library only, with no subprocesses, threads, sockets or network.
Per input: one CPU, one process, 1 GiB address space, 60 CPU seconds,
90 wall seconds, 16 MiB combined stdout/stderr. Temporary storage is unnecessary;
the target profile caps writable space at 64 MiB and 1024 entries. Formal
evaluation remains unavailable until that complete resource profile is enforced.
There is no speed score; resource limits are feasibility ceilings.

Run `python3 public_check.py` from `/workspace`. It executes only the public
examples in `examples/` and checks their published expected JSON. A nonzero
exit means at least one public example failed. Passing it is a sanity check,
not acceptance on the additional networks.

## Model scope

The protocol defines core/edge topology, weighted joint potentials, triple-minimum
and full-path diagnostics. Inference is exact and bounded, using the complete
joint law above and supplied priors. Declared links abstract trusted relationship
data; they do not perform ASPA object validation. No historical BGP data, Internet
accuracy claims or live routing are involved.
